localChanges: chore: lock the engine packages that let the Great Wall and the United Nations keep other leaders peaceful

log: The `DemandTribute` step after the handover isn't offered to a player `Pacified` towards the other (library-diplomacy), as Civ1's Great Wall and United Nations make every other leader towards their owner (civ-clone/web-renderer#30). In v474.05 the tribute demand needs the leader to be hostile, which either wonder rules out (`MeetWithKing.cs` ~L359, ~L0487).

Every other player is `Pacified` towards the owner of the Great Wall (until anyone discovers Gunpowder) or of the United Nations, so in a negotiation they make no demands of it, don't turn down its peace and end by offering it peace, and computer players don't break a peace with it (civ-clone/web-renderer#30).

v474.05 clears the leader's hostility in the human's parley for either wonder (`MeetWithKing.cs` ~L359), and keeps computer players who meet from going to war with the Great Wall's owner (`Segment_2517.cs` `F0_2517_0737`). Both act in every negotiation here, since computer players meet through the same one.
The Pyramids (civ-clone/web-renderer#33), Darwin's Voyage and the Apollo Program (civ1-spaceship) already have their effects.

`Pacified` (`Rule<[Player, Player], boolean>`) says whether a player is pacified towards another: it makes no demands of it and doesn't turn down its peace when they negotiate, and doesn't break a peace with it. `isPacified` is true if any match is. Civ1's Great Wall and United Nations supply it (civ-clone/civ1-wonder), the negotiation steps (civ-clone/civ1-diplomacy) and the AI (civ-clone/simple-ai-client) read it, for civ-clone/web-renderer#30.

`shouldBeHostile` is `shouldAttack` unless the player is `Pacified` towards the other (library-diplomacy), which Civ1's Great Wall and United Nations make every other leader towards their owner (civ-clone/web-renderer#30). Negotiation uses it in place of `shouldAttack`, so a pacified AI accepts the owner's peace, offers it peace and takes its knowledge however strong it is; so do sneak attacks, sneak captures and sneak thefts, so it never breaks a peace with the owner.
